column1: # *** THE MONTEVIDEO DISPENSATION SWEEP, RE-RUN ON COMPOUND SURNAMES - STARTED 12 OCTOBER 2026. ***
# The errand has stood 'ready' since September with a one-line reason: by 1900 Lerena is largely a
# MATERNAL surname inside compounds, so a surname-first sweep under-reads this family.
# *** THE REASON WAS HALF WRONG, AND WORKING OUT WHICH HALF IS THE USEFUL PART. *** This file is
# deliberately short and deliberately unfinished: it records what the gap actually is, proves the
# gap is not empty, and states plainly that the volume has NOT been paged. The errand stays open.
*** THE GAP THE OLD FORMULAE COULD NOT REACH ***
column2: the two formulae of 13 September - 'Lerena el impedimento' and 'Lerena feligresa'
column3: *** THEY CATCH LERENA-SECOND COMPOUNDS AND MISS LERENA-FIRST ONES ***
column4: The sweep that produced eight dispensations in seventy-six years was built on two phrases in which LERENA sits immediately before the next word.
column5: *** A COMPOUND WHERE LERENA COMES SECOND IS STILL CAUGHT *** - 'Gonzalez Lerena el impedimento' contains 'Lerena el impedimento'. *** A COMPOUND WHERE LERENA COMES FIRST IS NOT: *** 'Lerena Pelaez el impedimento' does not contain either phrase, because a surname has been pushed in between. *** That is the whole of the gap, and it is the opposite of the reason the errand was raised. *** The errand's premise was that Lerena is often a MATERNAL surname and so comes second - but it is precisely second-position Lerenas that the old sweep already caught.

column1: *** AND THE GAP IS NOT EMPTY ***
column2: full-text phrase searches for Lerena-first compounds, corpus-wide
column3: *** LERENA PELAEZ, LERENA LENGUAS and LERENA FERNANDEZ all return records; LERENA TRAIBEL returns none ***
column4: It was possible that clerks never wrote the compound at all - the archive's own compound test of 14 September found forty-three doublings and no genuine Uruguayan compound.
column5: *** THEY DO WRITE IT. *** 'Lerena Pelaez' appears in *** Santisima Trinidad, Trinidad, Flores. Confirmation Records 1891-1905 ***; 'Lerena Lenguas' in Santiago, Ciudad Vieja death records 1895-1900, La Union marriages 1902-1934 and Montevideo deaths 1910-1914; 'Lerena Fernandez' in Montevideo deaths 1972 and Lavalleja deaths 1924. *** Controlled: 'Lerena y Lerena' in the same form and session returns a full page of volumes, so a zero here is a zero. *** 'Lerena Traibel' is a true null corpus-wide - which is itself worth knowing, because the Traibel branch is the best-documented one in this archive.

column1: *** WHAT IS NOT DONE, AND SAYING SO ***
column2: the dispensation register itself, searched on the compound forms
column3: *** NOT YET RUN TO EXHAUSTION - THE ERRAND STAYS OPEN ***
column4: None of the compound searches above put the Marriage Dispensation Register in its top results, which is suggestive and is not proof.
column5: *** A TOP-RANKED LIST IS NOT A SEARCHED VOLUME. *** FamilySearch's full-text results paginate and rank, and this archive has twice recorded what happens when a ranked list is read as a filtered one - once at 290 records and once at *** herencia. *** So the honest position is: *** the gap is identified, the forms to use are now known, and the pages have not been turned. *** What remains is to page every result set for Lerena Pelaez, Lerena Lenguas, Lerena Fernandez, Lerena Villademoros, Lerena Juanico, Lerena Cardozo, Lerena Larriera and Lerena Razzetti, and look for the dispensation volume in each.

column3: *** THE IGLESIA DEL CORDON REGISTERS ARE IN THE FULL-TEXT CORPUS ***
column4: A separate errand has stood ready since September: search the Iglesia del Cordon, Montevideo. It had not been established that the volumes were machine-read at all.

The Cordon is also where film 007713392 image 2511 sits - the Cementerio del Cordon act this archive already read to kill a false compound. *** The errand is cheaper than it looked and can be run from this desk. ***
